guidelines.detail: refines EVT-03 (The reference places one 'Meal ready' intermediate catch event before both the receiving step and the buzzer step (M5, M9). The generated model instead used a waiting task (X1) and an event-based gateway with a separate 'Buzzer rings' catch event (X3, X4). The description names only one trigger for the continuation, so the extra gateway and alternative event are not supported. The wording is kept )

contradicts documentation rule COL-07 (The reference models the chef as a separate pool linked to the employee and guest pools by message flows, while the generated model put the employee and chef into lanes of one pool. The description states that the employee places orders with and informs the chef and that the chef reports back, which are message-based interactions between independent performers. Lanes cannot carry message flows, so)

same as LRN-061 (The generated model replaced the reported 'meal ready' catch event with an event-based gateway that adds a 'called by employee' alternative, which the reference does not model. The reference has a single catch event before the step it enables, and the description states the later call only as a reaction to a non-response, so it is not a competing trigger for the wait. The missing 'meal ready' even)

refines EVT-03 (The reference models the informed role's wait as an intermediate message catch event placed after the preceding step and fed by a message flow from the informing task (M9, C9, C6). The generated model instead uses an event-based gateway with a timer-like buzzer event and a separate end event (X3, X4, X12), and has no message flow into the wait. EVT-03 already says to use an intermediate catch even)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says the flow of a participant continues only after a stated occurrence happens, such as another party informing it that an item is ready, and the description names no alternative trigger for that continuation: Model that occurrence as one intermediate catch event on the waiting participant's flow, placed directly before the step it enables. Do not model the waiting itself as a task, and do not add an event-based gateway with an additional alternative catch event unless the description names several alternative triggers.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says the flow of a participant continues only after a stated occurrence happens, such as another party informing it that an item is ready, and the description names no alternative trigger for that continuation

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states one sentence in which a performer or performer group carries out two distinct activities joined by 'and', where the second activity responds to or resolves issues raised by the first: Model each of the two activities as its own task, in the order stated in the sentence, connected by a sequence flow. Do not merge them into one task whose label combines both actions, and do not drop either activity from the model.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description joins two or more distinct actions performed by the same actor in one sentence or one consecutive sequence (for example, an action on a system followed by an action on a person or an item, or preparing an item and then handing it to another party)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description has one role that performs its own sequence of steps and tells another role that a piece of work is finished, and the informed role's next step can only proceed after that notice arrives: Model the notice as a message flow from the informing task in the informing role's pool to an intermediate message catch event in the informed role's pool. Place that catch event after the informed role's own preceding step and before its next step. Do not model the wait as an event-based gateway, a send task, or a sequence flow from the other role. Do not add a separate event for a different message that the description does not mention.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description has one role that performs its own sequence of steps and tells another role that a piece of work is finished, and the informed role's next step can only proceed after that notice arrives

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that a participant is handed a device or notice that will later announce readiness, and that the participant then waits for that announcement before continuing to collect the result: When this holds, model the participant's wait as an intermediate catch event that is triggered by the later announcement, placed on the participant's path before the collection step. Model the announcing action on the other side as an intermediate throw event or a send task. Do not model the wait as a task, and do not connect the collection step directly without the catch event.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that a participant is handed a device or notice that will later announce readiness, and that the participant then waits for that announcement before continuing to collect the result

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description lists several consecutive actions by the same participant, each stated in its own sentence or clause and each acting on a different resource or counterpart (for example, recording an entry in a system, then collecting something from a counterpart, then setting up an item and handing it over, then informing another party), before the flow moves on: Model each such action as its own task in that participant's lane, in the order the description states them, connected by sequence flows. Do not drop any stated action, and do not fold it into a neighbouring task. Keep each action as a separate task even when the next action follows directly with no stated pause.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description lists several consecutive actions by the same participant, each stated in its own sentence or clause and each acting on a different resource or counterpart (for example, recording an entry in a system, then collecting something from a counterpart, then setting up an item and handing it over, then informing another party), before the flow moves on

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says one participant passes an order, a request, or the news of a finished item on to another participant, and the receiving participant's flow either begins with that passing-on or continues only after it: Model the sending side as a plain task in the sender's pool, not as a sendTask. Model the receiving side in the receiver's pool as a message start event if the passed-on item begins the receiver's process, or as an intermediate message catch event placed before the step it enables if the receiver's flow continues only after it. Connect the two with one message flow from the sending task to that event. Do not model the receiving side as a receiveTask, and do not pair a sendTask with a receiveTask for the same exchange.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says one participant passes an order, a request, or the news of a finished item on to another participant, and the receiving participant's flow either begins with that passing-on or continues only after it
